title: Lesson 1 · The sentence blueprint + to be
topic: Word order, no articles, and am/is/are

pattern.name: The sentence blueprint
notes: Subject always starts, verb always ends. Only the middle changes.
No a / an / the — Hindi doesn't use articles. Just drop them.
not = nahi, and it sits just before the verb section.
very = bahut (you also heard "bahot" — same word), placed before the word it boosts.
and = aur — works just like English: samosa aur pani puri.

grids.title: To be: am / is / are
rows: closest friends and little kids only

vocab.note: sits just before the verb section
also heard as bahot — same word; goes before the word it boosts

watch_out: (n) means a nasal sound, not a spoken N: hoo(n), hai(n). The vowel goes up your nose.
hai vs hain: hai comes from the throat, hain is the nasal one — that tiny difference is singular vs plural.
J and Z blur together in Hindi, and V and W are the same sound — that's why vo / wo is written both ways.
